subject: Life Skills
title: Chronos vs. Kairos
description: Learn Chronos vs. Kairos in one minute.

hook.text: Ancient Greeks had two words for time. We only have one. That missing word changes how you see your day.

buildup.text: Chronos is clock time — seconds, minutes, hours ticking relentlessly forward. It is the time on your wrist.

discovery.text: Kairos is the right moment — when conditions align and action feels effortless. Quality, not quantity of time.

twist.text: You can have eight free hours of chronos and waste them all. One kairos moment can change your whole week.

climax.text: Stop counting hours. Start noticing when you are in flow. Those kairos windows are where your best work lives.

punchline.text: Manage the clock. But chase the moment.

quiz.question: What does 'kairos' mean in ancient Greek?
